title: Pilot Activation Playbook and Technical Economics
author: Elena Schwartz
content:
Overview

This playbook explains how to structure a Redwood Inference pilot (aka Value Lab) for technical buyers and platform teams. It combines positioning, a competitive brief, concrete pricing options, activation steps, success metrics, and a short security FAQ tailored for pilot-stage conversations. Use this page when a customer asks for a hands-on evaluation to validate latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

Audience
- Sales engineers and AE executing pilots with mid-market and enterprise product/platform teams.
- Solutions and customer engineers who will run the initial integration and success metrics.

One-line pilot positioning
- "Run a 4–6 week Value Lab that proves Redwood reduces per-token inference cost by ~25–45% while meeting target latency for your production workload."

Target buyer personas and objectives
- Platform/Infra Owner: Validate deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and observability hooks.
- ML/Model Owner: Compare model variants, quantization impact, and quality regressions.
- Product Manager: Demonstrate user-facing latency and conversion impact.
- Security/Compliance: Validate data residency, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration.

Core messages for pilots
1) Predictable economics: transparent per-token cost modeling, batching/caching levers you can change during the pilot.
2) Production-first: same API and rollout controls used in production — no prototype lock-in.
3) Measurable quality: integrated evals and sample-level regressions with guardrails.
4) Fast time-to-validate: sample app + SDKs + pre-built metrics dashboards to prove outcomes within 4–6 weeks.

Competitive brief (high-level)
- Competitors often trade coverage for observability or require significant ops work to reach production SLAs. Redwood’s differentiator for pilots is a pre-baked observability + cost model and optional dedicated pilot capacity so customers get production-like behavior without full procurement.

Competitive snapshot (talking points table)
| Dimension | Redwood Pilot (Value Lab) | Typical Managed API | Self-hosted/Open-source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time to first meaningful metric | 3–7 days (sample app + dashboards) | 1–2 days but limited observability | 3–8 weeks setup + infra |
| Visibility into unit economics | Per-route token breakdown, batching/caching models, projection tool | Basic per-token billing | Ad hoc cost models |
| Production fidelity | Dedicated pilot pools or private deployment option | Shared noisy neighbor effects | Can be high but needs ops investment |
| Security & compliance | KMS, audit logs, VPC, SOC-ready artifacts for pilot | Varies; sometimes limited evidence | Depends on customer's infra |
| Model switching & rollback | Canary/A-B + automatic fallbacks | Usually manual | Manual or custom tooling |

Pilot offers and pricing guidance
- Standard Value Lab (recommended for most pilots): 4-week engagement, hosted pilot pool, up to 10M tokens included, pre-built dashboard, 2 SEs (30 hours total) for integration and tuning. Price: credit-based promo or reduced pilot fee (examples below).
- Dedicated Proof-of-Value: 6-week engagement with reserved GPU capacity, model quantization testing, extended observability retention. Recommended for regulated workloads.
- Hybrid (Private test): Short on-prem or VPC deployment with limited data egress; pricing includes airgap packaging and 2-week on-site/remote operations support.

Sample pricing scenarios (guidance, subject to discounts)
| Offer | Duration | Included tokens | SE hours | Typical commercial anchor | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Standard Value Lab (pilot credit) | 4 weeks | 10M | 30 | $15k list pilot fee (often waived) | Good for fast proof |
| Dedicated PoV | 6 weeks | 50M | 80 | $45k | For enterprise/regulatory needs |
| Hybrid Private Test | 4–6 weeks | 20M | 60 | $60k + packaging | Includes on-prem package |

Pricing mechanics and economics to highlight
- Unit models: show per-1k-token run rate before/after batching and cache: e.g., baseline managed API: $0.60 / 1k tokens vs Redwood optimized pilot: $0.22–0.40 / 1k tokens depending on workload and cache hit-rate.
- Cost levers: batch size, KV/prefix caching, quantization profile. Provide customers with a short spreadsheet template to project 12-month run rate under multiple adoption scenarios.
- Upside protection: offer an "economic guardrail" clause in pilots that maps observed production token mix to committed pricing conversation.

Activation checklist (step-by-step)
1) Kickoff (day 0): introduce teams, confirm success metrics, share sample dataset, sign pilot MOU.
2) Architecture choose (day 1–3): hosted vs dedicated pilot pool vs VPC test. Confirm network routes, IP allowlists, and KMS plan.
3) Integration (day 3–10): SDK integration, sample app deployment, enable tracing tags and per-request metadata.
4) Baseline run (day 10–14): run representative traffic (10–20k requests) to capture p50/p95 latency, token distribution, and quality baselines.
5) Optimization & tuning (day 14–28): enable batching, try quantized model variants, enable prefix/KV caching. Track cost delta per experiment.
6) Validation (day 28–35): run A/B test or canary to validate user-facing metrics and guardrails.
7) Wrap-up & next steps (week 6): deliver final report, recommended production configuration, and commercial proposal.

Success metrics to include in pilot SOW
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-turn queries with seq_len <= 256 (or customer-defined).
- Cost target: demonstrable >= 20% reduction in per-unit inference cost vs customer's current baseline.
- Quality delta: automated evals show <= 1.5% regression on critical prompt set (or stakeholder-approved threshold).
- Reliability: availability >= 99.5% during pilot window for routed requests.

Observability & dashboard deliverables
- Per-route token & cost breakdown (CSV export).
- Latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99) by model variant.
- Request traces mapped to model variant and caching state.
- Quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

Customer case study (pilot example): NorthBridge Retail (fictional condensed summary)
- Objective: replace a rule-based search-reranker with semantic reranking for product discovery while keeping p95 < 300ms.
- Approach: 4-week Value Lab using hosted dedicated pool, evaluated two quantized Llama-family variants and prefix caching.
- Outcome: 38% reduction in per-interaction inference cost, p95 improved from 420ms to 280ms, A/B showed a 4.2% lift in conversion for product searches.
- Deliverables: final runbook, recommended production config (dedicated pool + 2-stage reranker), and a commercial term sheet for annual reserved capacity.

Security FAQ for prospects in pilot stage
Q: Will my customer data be stored or used to train models?
A: No. By default, Redwood’s hosted pilot mode does not use customer data to improve public models. For private deployments we provide an air-gapped option.

Q: How do you handle keys and secrets?
A: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM, temporary access tokens scoped per-pilot, and audit logs for all key operations.

Q: Can we run the pilot in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes — we offer hybrid private tests and on-prem packaging for pilots that require no egress. These require a short checklist for network and patch levels.

Q: What evidence do you provide for compliance reviews?
A: Pilot packages include SOC-style artifacts: architecture diagrams, data flow descriptions, sample audit logs, and an attestation checklist. For regulated customers we add a demo of KMS bindings.

Battlecard: common competitor objections + rebuttals
- Objection: "We already use a managed API, it's cheaper and faster to iterate."
  Rebuttal: "Managed APIs can be fast to start but often lack the unit economics visibility and production fidelity needed at scale. Our pilot model shows end-to-end cost and SLO tradeoffs and gives you knobs you can tune immediately (batching, cache, quantization)."

- Objection: "Self-hosting gives us the lowest cost."
  Rebuttal: "Self-hosting can offer low marginal compute cost, but total cost of ownership (ops, reliability, observability) and time-to-production are substantial. Redwood pilots provide production-like fidelity without long-term ops investment, and we can hand off an ops runbook for an eventual migration."

Slide deck outline (10 slides recommended)
1) Title & objectives for the Value Lab
2) Executive summary: expected outcomes and anchor metrics
3) Pilot scope & timeline (include success metrics)
4) Architecture options (hosted/dedicated/private) with recommended path
5) Economics: baseline vs projected post-optimization (sample spreadsheet excerpt)
6) Observability & quality monitoring demo screenshots
7) Security/compliance evidence checklist
8) Sample results (if available from baseline run)
9) Commercial options & next steps
10) Appendix: technical checklist & escalation contacts

Ownership and escalation
- Pilot owner (Commercial): AE assigned to the account (named in SOW).
- Technical owner: Solutions Engineer (SE) — typically SE + 1 customer engineer.
- Escalation: for infra/perf issues, engage Eng-Serving-Runtime on-call channel and Product-Infra lead (contact list included in appendix).

Templates and artifacts to attach to SOW
- Sample MOU (pilot statement of work).
- Sample cost projection spreadsheet (CSV).
- Integration checklist (network, KMS, logging).
- Sample prompt set and eval harness to run automated quality checks.

Next steps for AEs/SEs
1) Use this playbook to align internal stakeholders and draft the pilot MOU.
2) Book a 30-minute kickoff slot with customer and attach the integration checklist.
3) Deliver baseline report (week 2) and schedule optimization showback (week 3–4).
